history.value: A fine-tune burst of one-turn games buys back a mechanic the net misreads inside the search horizon, and nothing a read can see elsewhere. It works on powers that punish an action (sharp2 +0.054 to +0.084 wins at about 100-400 games, carrying to Thorns and WeakOnHit; measurement/adaptation-curve, measurement/adaptation-transfer) and survives two-turn search at about a third (measurement/adapted-two@elites). It does not work on plain numbers (measurement/stat-burst@one-turn), on growth past the horizon (Ritual 2, measurement/rate-columns@ritual2), or on whole official bosses the net never trained on: the Guardian gains about +0.026 over bursts on other content and Hexaghost nothing at 400 or 1600 games (measurement/unseen-boss-burst@replay), although the second turn of search wins +0.083 more Hexaghost fights on the same decks (measurement/depth-by-boss@replay), so there is play to learn that outcome labels at the student's own depth do not carry (cause/teacher-equals-student). Planning rules: an enemy made of familiar parts has no cost a burst can recover, so goal 1's benches spend their fights on unseen mechanics; a boss burst is no goal-2 candidate. Exits: inputs that show the state deciding a boss (its move schedule, HP-scaled attacks, Burn rows), or a boss read where a burst beats the bursts on other content by 0.05 or more one turn deep.
